summary:
We developed an interactive, educational, mission-based space exploration video game that uses Earth as a natural laboratory to study the geological, topographic, and environmental conditions of Mars and the Moon.

The game addresses the challenge by transforming real scientific data provided by NASA into eight dynamic missions (four about Mars and four about the Moon), where students take on the role of space researchers. By overcoming these scientific challenges, they unlock a final mission to prepare a field expedition and explore, on a 3D Earth globe, nine analog sites across the American continent with features similar to both celestial bodies.

This project is important because it democratizes science outreach and turns complex information into an accessible and engaging learning experience. It encourages critical thinking and curiosity among high school students in Mexico, proving that space science is not out of reach and that exploring other worlds starts by studying our own planet.
details: Our project consists of developing an educational space exploration video game that uses Earth as a natural laboratory to understand the characteristics of Mars and the Moon. The player takes on the role of a space agency researcher and must complete eight scientific missions, four for each celestial body, solving challenges to gather data and unlock a final mission: preparing a field expedition under simulated extraterrestrial conditions. As a result, the video game identifies eleven sites across the American continent with geographic and topographic features similar to the environments studied, displayed through a 3D Earth globe. Its main benefit is transforming scientific information into an interactive experience that makes learning easier and sparks curiosity about space exploration. Its expected impact is to serve as a teaching tool for high school students in Mexico, promoting critical thinking and science outreach. To build it, we used HTML and Claude Code as a programming support tool, relying exclusively on data and resources provided by NASA during the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 hackathon. Its creativity lies in combining gamification, scientific research, and geographic exploration, taking into account data accuracy, the features of the selected sites, and educational accessibility for students.
